action: Play / stop the pattern
goal: Start the sequencer; press PLAY again to stop.

citation.quote: Plays the pattern. Press the button again to stop playback.

action: Select a pattern (bank 1–4, number 1–16)
goal: Recall any of the 64 patterns: hold PATTERN and tap pads 1–4 for the bank, release, then tap pads 1–16 for the number.
steps: Hold PATTERN and press pad 1–4 to choose the bank.
Release PATTERN and press pad 1–16 to choose the pattern number.

citation.quote: Hold down the [PATTERN] button and press the [1]–[4] pads to select a bank.

action: Queue the next pattern during playback
goal: Pick a new pattern while one is playing; it starts automatically when the current pattern finishes, for seamless live switching.

citation.quote: Once the current pattern finishes playing, the next pattern you reserved automatically begins playing.

action: Scroll through patterns with the knob
goal: With the PATTERN button lit (pattern select mode), turn TEMPO/VALUE to step through patterns.

citation.quote: Turn the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob to select a pattern.

action: Set the tempo (BPM)
goal: On the main screen, turn TEMPO/VALUE to change the tempo.

citation.quote: Turn the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob to set the tempo.

action: Fine-tune the tempo in 0.1 BPM steps
goal: Match another device or a track exactly by adjusting the tempo in tenths of a BPM.

citation.quote: The value can be adjusted (fine-tuned) in steps of 0.1.

action: Shift the keyboard octave (−4 to +4)
goal: Reach bass or lead registers on the 16 keyboard pads.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [OCT-] [OCT+] pads.

action: Reset the octave to zero
goal: Jump back to the default octave instead of tapping OCT− / OCT+ several times.

citation.quote: By holding down the [SHIFT] button and pressing the [OCT-] pad and the [OCT+] pad, you can reset the octave setting (to zero).

action: Latch held notes (keyboard hold)
goal: Keep notes or chords sounding after you lift your fingers — handy for drones and pads.

citation.quote: Turns the keyboard pad hold function on/off.

action: Transpose keyboard and sequencer (key transpose)
goal: Move the whole pattern up or down (−60 to +60 semitones), e.g. to follow a chord change.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [STEP] (KEY TRANSPOSE) button.

action: Transpose live by tapping a key (±12)
goal: In the key-transpose screen, hold SHIFT and tap a keyboard pad to jump straight to that transposition while the pattern plays.

citation.quote: At this time, you can also hold down the [SHIFT] button and press a keyboard pad to make this setting within a range of -12 to +12.

action: Set a pattern’s volume (vOL)
goal: Balance levels between patterns so switching live doesn’t jump in loudness.

citation.quote: Sets the pattern’s volume.

action: Program steps TR-style with the step pads
goal: With REC unlit, light STEP and tap pads 1–16 to add a note on that step; tap again to delete it.
caveat: REC must be unlit for step-pad input. New steps get note C5 — change it with step editing.
steps: Make sure REC is unlit and press STEP so it lights.
Tap pads 1–16 to add (or delete) a note on each step.

citation.quote: A note (C5) is input to the step you selected, and the step pad lights up.

goal: Edit patterns longer than 16 steps by paging with the ◄ / ► keys.

citation.quote: While the [STEP] button is lit, use the [PORTA ON] (<) [PORTA TIME] (>) pads to switch between pages.

action: Set the pattern length (last step 1–64)
goal: Make odd-length loops or extend a pattern up to 64 steps.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [4] (LAST).

action: Record in real time
goal: Arm REC, start PLAY and play the keyboard; the pattern loops so you can keep overdubbing notes.
caveat: Turn on the count-in and metronome (SHIFT + PAD 15 MENU) to record in time more easily.

citation.quote: The display indicates “rEc”, and recording begins.

action: Clear notes (whole pattern or selected step)
goal: Wipe the sequence to start over — or only the selected step’s notes when a step is selected.
caveat: Press pad 1 (EXIT) instead of ENTER to cancel. Motions are kept; clear them with CLEAR MOTION.

citation.quote: Erases all notes in the selected pattern. When a step is selected, this deletes only the notes for that step.

action: Copy a step
goal: Grab one step’s notes and data so you can paste it elsewhere in the pattern.
steps: Press REC so it lights; the step number is shown.
Turn TEMPO/VALUE to choose the source step.
Hold STEP, press pad 15 (MENU), select “COPY” and press pad 2 (ENTER).

citation.quote: “donE” appears, and the data for the selected step is ready to be pasted.

action: Paste a copied step
goal: Overwrite the selected step with the step you copied.
steps: Copy a step first (COPY).
With REC lit, turn TEMPO/VALUE to the destination step.
Hold STEP, press pad 15 (MENU), select “PStE” and press pad 2 (ENTER).

citation.quote: “donE” appears, and the data of the copy source step overwrites the selected step.

action: Insert an empty step
goal: Push everything after the selected step one step later — quick way to shift a phrase.
steps: Press REC so it lights; the step number is shown.
Turn TEMPO/VALUE to the step where the gap should go.
Hold STEP, press pad 15 (MENU), select “InSr” and press pad 2 (ENTER).

citation.quote: “donE” is shown, and the empty step is inserted into the selected step, which shifts all steps afterwards by one step forward.

action: Double the pattern (copy all steps after the end)
goal: Turn a 16-step loop into 32 steps with an identical copy, ready for variations.

citation.quote: “donE” appears, and the steps from step 1 through the last step are copied after the last step, doubling the length.

action: Change the step length (pattern scale)
goal: Switch between 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 and triplet steps for half-time, double-time or triplet feels.

citation.quote: You can also edit the value by holding down the [PATTERN] button and turning the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob.

action: Add shuffle / swing
goal: Shift the off-beat steps for a swung groove.

citation.quote: Configures the shuffle settings (-90–0–90).

action: Push or pull probability for the whole pattern
goal: Thin out or fill in a generative pattern live: the master probability is added to every step’s own probability.
caveat: Only steps whose own probability is 99 or lower are affected; steps at 100 always play.

citation.quote: You can also set this by holding down the [STEP] button and turning the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob.

action: Loop selected steps live (step loop)
goal: Repeat one or more steps during playback as a stutter effect; press PATTERN to exit.
steps: Start playback with PLAY.
Hold SHIFT and press PATTERN (it blinks).
Keep pressing the step pads you want to repeat.
Press PATTERN to exit.

citation.quote: The [PATTERN] button blinks, and the unit enters step loop mode.

action: Metronome mode shortcut
goal: A shortcut to the metronome mode setting (Off / Rec / Rec&Play), listed in the manual’s shortcut table.

citation.quote: [SHIFT] button + [●] (REC) button Metronome mode(Ver.1.02)

action: Metronome mode and level (menu)
goal: Choose when the click plays — Off, Rec only or Rec&Play — and set its level (Ntr.L).

citation.quote: rC.PL (Rec&Play) Turns on during recording and playback

action: Set a count-in for recording
goal: Get 2–4 beats of lead-in before real-time recording starts.

citation.quote: Sets the length (the number of beats) of the count-in for recording.

action: Select a step to edit (STEP + REC lit)
goal: With STEP and REC both lit, press a step pad (or turn TEMPO/VALUE) to pick the step you want to edit.

citation.quote: Press a step pad to select the step to edit.

action: Edit a step’s note, velocity, gate, probability or sub steps
goal: Hold a step pad and tap D-MOTION to cycle through its data, then turn TEMPO/VALUE to edit the value shown.

citation.quote: When you press the [D-MOTION] button while holding down a step pad, the display switches in the following order.

action: Change a step’s note (pitch)
goal: Fix wrong notes or move a whole chord: the lowest chord note is shown and the others follow.

citation.quote: If a chord has been input, the lowest note number in the chord is shown.

action: Set per-step velocity (accents)
goal: Add accents and dynamics with a velocity of 1–127 per step.

citation.quote: v.100 Sets the velocity.

action: Set gate time (note length) per step
goal: Shorten notes for staccato, or set 100 to tie into the next step when it holds the same note.

citation.quote: When this is set to 100 and the same note number has been input for the next step, a tie is played.

action: Set per-step probability
goal: Make individual steps play only some of the time (1–100) for evolving, generative lines.

citation.quote: Sets the probability for notes to play back.

action: Ratchet a step with sub steps
goal: Split a step into several hits and choose which ones sound, for rolls and ratchets.
caveat: Applies to every note in the step and has no effect on empty steps or steps in the middle of a tie.

citation.quote: Divides up the step to play.

action: Tie a step into the next step
goal: Extend a note across steps for long bass notes and legato lines.
caveat: You can’t tie into a step that already contains a note.

citation.quote: To input a tie that extends to the next step, press the [HOLD] button while holding down the step pad of the step whose length you wish to change.

action: Enter chords on a step with the keyboard
goal: With STEP unlit and REC lit, choose a step with TEMPO/VALUE and toggle up to four keyboard notes on it.

citation.quote: Press the note on the keyboard pad corresponding to the note you want to play, to make it light up.

action: Edit steps while the pattern plays
goal: Light STEP and REC, start playback, then pick steps with TEMPO/VALUE or the pads to edit them while you listen.

citation.quote: Editing a step while checking what you played

action: Set velocity / gate per chord note
goal: While editing a chord step (REC lit, STEP unlit), give each chord note its own velocity and gate.

citation.quote: Hold down the keyboard pad of the note that contains the performance data you want to change, and press the [D-MOTION] button to select the performance data to edit.

action: Tie a single chord note into the next step
goal: Hold one note of a chord over the next step while the others change.

citation.quote: After the tie is inputted, the unit automatically advances to the next step and the step number is shown in the display.

action: Enter step notes from a MIDI keyboard
goal: Hold a step pad and play the note on a connected keyboard instead of editing the note number.

citation.quote: When an external keyboard is connected, you can also input notes by pressing the step pads on this unit and then playing the desired note on your external keyboard.

action: Record a motion on one step
goal: Lock a knob value to a single step (e.g. open the filter on step 9 only).

citation.quote: Hold down the step pad and turn a knob to register the motion.

action: Record knob motion in real time
goal: Capture filter sweeps and other moves while the pattern loops.
caveat: Up to eight parameters plus pitch bend per pattern; “FULL” means the slots are used up. MIDI CC and pitch bend are only recorded in real time.

citation.quote: Turn the knob while you play to register a motion.

action: Add a motion to the selected step
goal: In REC step mode, select a step with TEMPO/VALUE and turn a knob to store its value on that step.

citation.quote: Turn the knob to register a motion.

action: Clear motions (whole pattern or selected step)
goal: Remove recorded knob automation; when a step is selected only that step’s motions go.

citation.quote: Erases all motions in the selected pattern. When a step is selected, this deletes only the motions for that step.

action: Erase one knob’s motion only
goal: While “CLr.N” blinks, turn the knob whose motion you want gone — only that parameter is erased.

citation.quote: If “CLr.N” is blinking while the unit is waiting and you turn a knob, the parameter for only that knob is deleted.

action: Check a knob’s value without changing it
goal: See the stored value — for example while a motion plays — without overwriting the sound.

citation.quote: Operate while holding down the [STEP] button or operate while holding down the [PATTERN] button (Ver. 1.02)

action: Check a SHIFT-layer value without changing it
goal: Display the hidden SHIFT parameter of a knob (fine tune, delay time…) without editing it.

citation.quote: Operate while holding down the [PATTERN] and [STEP] buttons

action: Choose Mono / Unison / Poly / Chord
goal: Set the voice mode; Poly plays up to four notes at once.

citation.quote: Lets you play more than one tone at the same time (up to four voices).

action: Fatten a sound with Unison mode
goal: Stack the voices on every note for a thick mono lead or bass.

citation.quote: Stacks multiple tones to play a layered note.

action: One-finger chords (Chord mode)
goal: Every key plays a chord: switch voices 2–4 on/off and transpose each by up to ±12 semitones.

citation.quote: Press pad [2] (ENTER) while “Chd” is shown in the display to configure the following parameters.

action: Last-note or low-note priority (n.Pri)
goal: In Mono, Unison or Chord mode, choose whether the last or the lowest held key sounds.

citation.quote: You can use the Note Priority setting (“n.Pri” in the menu) to select between giving priority to either the last note (LASt) or the lowest note

action: Turn the arpeggiator on
goal: Hold a chord on the keyboard and let the S-1 arpeggiate it.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [8] (ARPEGGIO ON).

action: Toggle the arp on/off in one move
goal: Tap pad 8 again while holding SHIFT to flip the arpeggiator on or off without the knob.

citation.quote: Press pad [8] (ARPEGGIO ON) repeatedly while holding down the [SHIFT] button to toggle the arpeggio on/off.

action: Choose the arp pattern (Up, Down, Up&Down, Random, 2-octave)
goal: Change the direction and range of the arpeggio.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [9] (ARPEGGIO TYPE).

action: Set the arp rate (1/4 to 1/32, triplets)
goal: Speed the arpeggio up or down in tempo-synced note values.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [10] (ARPEGGIO RATE).

action: Latch the arpeggio with HOLD
goal: Keep the arp running hands-free; play new keys to change the chord.

citation.quote: When you press the [HOLD] button to make it light up while an arpeggio is playing, the arpeggio keeps playing even after you take your finger off the keyboard pad.

action: Glide between notes (portamento Off / On / Auto)
goal: Slide smoothly from note to note; Auto glides only when you play legato.
caveat: With the arpeggiator running, Auto only glides when ENV TRG is set to Gate.

citation.quote: Portamento is an effect that makes one pitch glide smoothly into another.

action: Set the glide time
goal: Make the portamento slide faster or slower (0–255).

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [PORTA TIME] pad.

action: Reach the hidden SHIFT parameter of a knob
goal: Many knobs have a second parameter (fine tune, delay time, pulse width…) when turned with SHIFT held.

citation.quote: By turning the knobs while holding down the [SHIFT] button, you can access tone parameters that are different from the normal parameters.

action: Make the sound match the knob positions (manual)
goal: Apply every top-panel knob position to the tone at once — the quickest start for sound design from scratch.
caveat: Parameters set with SHIFT (the knob assignment layer) are not changed.

citation.quote: Press the [SHIFT] + [HOLD] buttons to enter manual mode.

action: Draw your own waveform (OSC DRAW)
goal: Design a custom 16-step single-cycle wave and hear it through the square-wave level knob.
caveat: Pulse width modulation is not applied to a drawn waveform.
steps: Hold SHIFT and press pad 5 (OSC DRAW).
Turn TEMPO/VALUE to choose a parameter (switch, form or multiply) and press pad 2 (ENTER).
Turn TEMPO/VALUE to edit; set the switch to STEP or SLOPE to use your waveform.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [5] (OSC DRAW).

action: Edit the drawn waveform step by step
goal: In the Form screen, hold a pad (one of 16 wave steps) and turn TEMPO/VALUE to set its height from −100 to 100.

citation.quote: You can create original waveforms by dividing a single waveform cycle into 16 steps and individually editing the volume for each step.

action: Switch OSC DRAW (Off / Step / Slope) from the saw knob
goal: Flip between the plain square wave and your drawn waveform without opening the menu.

citation.quote: You can also edit the values by turning the OSCILLATOR [ (sawtooth wave level)] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Sweep OSC DRAW Multiply from the square knob
goal: With OSC DRAW on, repeat the drawn wave within each cycle for brighter, octave-jumping tones.
caveat: When OSC DRAW is switched off, the same move adjusts pulse width instead.

citation.quote: You can also edit the value by turning the OSCILLATOR [ (square wave level)] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Leave the waveform / chop-pattern editor
goal: The pads edit wave steps in these screens, so use SHIFT + pad 1 to return to the parameter list.

citation.quote: To exit, hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [1] (EXIT).

action: Chop the waveform for edgy harmonics (OSC CHOP)
goal: Cut slices out of each oscillator waveform to emphasise overtones and get metallic tones.

citation.quote: You can chop the waveforms that are generated by the oscillator, and emphasize their harmonics (overtones).

action: Cut slices out of the wave (chop pattern)
goal: In a chop-pattern screen, toggle any of the 16 slices of the waveform; each of the four waveforms has its own pattern.

citation.quote: Press pads [1]–[16] corresponding to the steps you want to edit, which makes the pads go dark.

action: Sweep OSC CHOP Overtone from the OSC LFO knob
goal: Dial the chop intensity in real time — great for motion recording.
caveat: With Overtone at 0 the chop pattern has no effect.

citation.quote: You can also edit the value by turning the OSCILLATOR [LFO] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Sweep OSC CHOP Comb from the SUB knob
goal: Repeat the chop pattern within each cycle for metallic, comb-like tones.

citation.quote: You can also edit the value by turning the OSCILLATOR [SUB] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Choose the pulse-width modulation source
goal: Animate the square wave from the LFO or envelope, or set a fixed width manually.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [PWM SRC] pad.

action: Set pulse width / PWM depth
goal: Set the fixed pulse width, or how far the LFO/envelope moves it.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [PWM DEPTH] pad.

action: Sweep pulse width from the square knob
goal: Change the square wave’s width by hand — record it as a motion for movement.
caveat: With OSC DRAW switched on, this move controls Multiply instead.

citation.quote: OSC PULSE WIDTH ([SHIFT] button + [PWM DEPTH] pad) ([SHIFT] +OSCILLATOR [ ] knob)

action: Choose the sub-oscillator octave
goal: Pick −1 octave, −2 octaves or the asymmetrical −2 octave wave for the sub.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [SUB OCT] pad.

action: Switch pink / white noise
goal: Choose the noise colour straight from the NOISE knob.
caveat: When Riser Mode is on, SHIFT + NOISE controls the riser instead.

citation.quote: NOISE MODE ([SHIFT] button + pad [15] (MENU): Noise Mode) ([SHIFT] + OSCILLATOR [NOISE] knob)

action: Fine-tune the oscillator (±1 octave)
goal: Detune the S-1 against other instruments or patterns.

citation.quote: You can turn the [RANGE] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button to alter the pitch within a ±1 octave range

action: Make the filter track the keyboard
goal: Keep high notes as bright as low ones; 255 makes the cutoff follow the pitch exactly.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [7] (FILTER KYBD).

action: Set filter key tracking from the filter ENV knob
goal: Adjust keyboard follow without leaving the panel.

citation.quote: FILTER KEYBOARD FOLLOW ([SHIFT] button + pad [7] (FILTER KYBD) pad) ([SHIFT] button +FILTER [ENV] knob)

action: Set the envelope trigger (LFO / Gate / Gate+Trig)
goal: Retrigger the envelope on every key, only on non-legato notes, or repeatedly with the LFO.

citation.quote: triG (Gate+Trig): The envelope is triggered each time you press a key.

action: Gate or envelope for the amp (AMP mode)
goal: Use a simple organ-like gate, or let the ADSR knobs shape the volume.

citation.quote: GAtE (Gate): Sound is played at a set volume only while a key is played.

combo: PWM SRC / SUB OCT / ENV TRG / AMP / POLY / PORTA ON (repeatedly)
action: Cycle values by tapping the key again
goal: While holding SHIFT, tap the same key repeatedly to step through its settings — no knob needed.

citation.quote: You can switch between the values in order by repeatedly pressing the following pads while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Switch LFO Normal / Fast from the RATE knob
goal: Fast mode speeds the LFO cycle up to an extreme degree for more intense modulation.

citation.quote: LFO MODE ([SHIFT] button + pad [15] (MENU): LFO Mode) ([SHIFT] +LFO [RATE] knob)

action: Sync the LFO to tempo from the WAVE FORM knob
goal: Lock wobbles and tremolo to the beat; RATE then picks a note length.

citation.quote: LFO WAVE FORM (#12) LFO SYNC (“S”, #106) (Ver.1.02)

action: Restart the LFO on every note (LFO.K)
goal: Make each note start from the same point of the LFO cycle.

citation.quote: Sets whether to reset the LFO when a note sounds.

action: Set the delay time from the DELAY knob
goal: Dial echo timing by hand; DELAY alone sets the level.

citation.quote: You can set the delay time by turning the [DELAY] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Delay settings: tempo sync, time, feedback, filters
goal: Sync the delay to tempo, set feedback, and low/high-cut the repeats.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press [13] (DELAY) pad.

action: Set the reverb time from the REVERB knob
goal: Lengthen or shorten the tail by hand; REVERB alone sets the level.

citation.quote: Adjust the reverb length (time) by turning the [REVERB] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Reverb type and settings (room, hall, plate, spring…)
goal: Choose the reverb type and set pre-delay, filters and density.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press pad [14] (REVERB).

action: Add chorus (types 1–4)
goal: Thicken pads and leads; type 3 behaves like a fast rotary speaker.

citation.quote: This effect adds a tiny amount of pitch modulation, creating a more spacious and thicker sound.

action: Keep FX tails when switching patterns
goal: Use global (system) delay/reverb so tails ring on across pattern changes.

citation.quote: As the system settings are given priority, the tail of the delay/reverb continues to sound even while you switch between patterns.

action: Delay knob as send (Pre) or return (Post)
goal: Pre lets repeats ring out when you turn DELAY down — dub-style throws; Post mutes them instantly.

citation.quote: With the “PrE” setting, the delay sound fades out smoothly when you turn down the [DELAY] knob

action: Switch Riser Mode (Off / Sync / Quiv / QvPn)
goal: Turn the NOISE knob into a riser/downer generator for build-ups — without opening the menu.

citation.quote: You can switch between Riser Mode settings each time you press pad [1] (EXIT) and pad [2] (ENTER) at the same time while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

action: Play the riser / downer with the NOISE knob
goal: With Riser Mode on, sweep NOISE from minimum to the middle for a rise, then on to maximum for a falling downer.

citation.quote: Use the [NOISE] knob to control both the riser and downer effects.

action: Reposition the riser silently
goal: Move the NOISE knob without sounding the riser, ready to start the effect from any point.

citation.quote: You can change the knob position without outputting the riser sound if you hold down the [SHIFT] button while turning the [NOISE] knob

action: Pre-set the riser, then drop it on SHIFT release
goal: Prepare the downer while the riser keeps going, then switch the instant you let go of SHIFT.

citation.quote: After you turn the [NOISE] knob to a setting besides minimum or maximum while holding down the [SHIFT] button and then release the [SHIFT] button, the riser sound is output immediately according to the knob position.

action: Tilt to tweak the sound (D-MOTION)
goal: Hold D-MOTION and tilt the S-1 back/forth (pitch) or left/right (roll) to modulate the assigned parameters; release to snap back.
caveat: Grip both sides firmly and make sure connected cables aren’t bent too much.

citation.quote: While holding down the [D-MOTION] button, tilt the unit back and forth (pitch) or left-right (roll).

action: Assign what pitch and roll tilt control
goal: Map roll and pitch to modulation, cutoff, resonance, pitch bend, pan, expression, or delay/reverb level.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [D-MOTION] button.

action: Make D-MOTION latch instead of momentary (d.Lat)
goal: Toggle tilt control on and off with one press so both hands are free to tilt.

citation.quote: On: D-MOTION toggles between ON/OFF each time you press the button (latch operation).

action: Set the pitch-bend range for D-MOTION / MIDI (bnd.o)
goal: Decide how far D-MOTION or MIDI pitch bend moves the oscillator (120 = ±1 oct, 240 = ±2 oct).

citation.quote: Use the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob to select “bnd.o”, and press pad [2] (ENTER).

action: Set vibrato depth for D-MOTION / MIDI modulation (Nod.d)
goal: Control how strong the LFO vibrato or growl is when modulation comes from tilting or a mod wheel.

citation.quote: Use the [TEMPO/VALUE] knob to select “Nod.d”, and press pad [2] (ENTER).

action: Save the pattern (or all patterns)
goal: Write the sequence and sound to memory: choose “Ptn” for the current pattern or “ALL” for every pattern.

citation.quote: Once the power is turned off, any unsaved patterns are reset to their last saved state.

action: Copy the pattern to another slot
goal: Duplicate a pattern before making a variation of it.

citation.quote: Copies the current pattern to a specified pattern.

action: Initialize a pattern (blank sequence and sound)
goal: Start from a clean slate for sound design or a new sequence.
caveat: Nothing is stored until you WRITE — turning the power off brings back the previous state.

citation.quote: This shows how to initialize the currently selected pattern (sequence and tone).

action: Revert the pattern to its last save
goal: Throw away all unsaved changes to the current pattern.

citation.quote: This shows how to restore the currently selected pattern to its last saved state.

action: Reload just the sound (one-move shortcut)
goal: Undo knob tweaks after a jam while keeping your edited sequence.

citation.quote: Press the [SHIFT] button, pad [1] (EXIT) and the [POLY] pad at the same time to reload the sound.

action: Reload just the sequence
goal: Restore the saved notes and motions while keeping the current sound.

citation.quote: rL.Sq (Reload Sequence): The performance data of the selected pattern is restored to its last saved state.

action: Back up all data to a computer
goal: Keep your patterns safe before experiments, firmware updates or a factory reset.
steps: Connect the S-1 to your computer by USB.
Hold PLAY while turning the power on; the drive takes 1–2 minutes to appear.
Copy everything in the BACKUP folder, then eject the drive.

citation.quote: The backup files are located in the “BACKUP” folder on the “S-1” drive.

action: Restore a backup from a computer
goal: Load a previous backup back onto the S-1.
steps: Start the S-1 in drive mode (hold PLAY while powering on) and connect it by USB.
Copy the backup files into the RESTORE folder and eject the drive.
Press HOLD to restore, then turn the S-1 off when “dOnE” appears.

citation.quote: Copy the backup files to the “RESTORE” folder on the “S-1” drive.

action: Factory reset
goal: Return the S-1 to its factory state.
caveat: This erases your patterns — back up first. To cancel, turn the power off instead of pressing D-MOTION.

citation.quote: While holding down the [HOLD] button, turn on the power.

action: Open the menu, pick an item, confirm or exit
goal: Every menu setting works the same way: TEMPO/VALUE selects, pad 2 (ENTER) confirms, pad 1 (EXIT) backs out.

citation.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press step pad [15] (MENU).

action: Change values in bigger jumps
goal: Scroll through long value ranges faster while editing a parameter.

citation.quote: Use this knob with the [SHIFT] button to fine-tune the tempo or to make larger adjustments to the parameter values.

action: Set the MIDI channel (CH)
goal: Match the S-1 to your sequencer or DAW track.

citation.quote: Specifies the MIDI transmit/receive channel.

action: Choose the clock source (Auto / Int / MIDI / USB)
goal: Follow a DAW or drum machine, or run on the internal clock.
caveat: A cable in the SYNC IN jack always takes priority over this setting.

citation.quote: Sets which synchronization signal is used by this unit.

action: Set sync pulses per beat (S.cLk)
goal: Match the SYNC IN/OUT pulse rate (1–24 per beat) to analog-clocked gear.

citation.quote: Sets the number of sync clocks per beat.

action: MIDI Thru on/off
goal: Pass incoming MIDI on to the next device in the chain.

citation.quote: Sets whether to output the messages that are input from the MIDI IN jack to the MIDI OUT jack (ON) or not (OFF).

action: Change patterns via MIDI program change
goal: Let a DAW or sequencer switch S-1 patterns (rxPc); send them with txPc and set the channel with Pc.Ch.

citation.quote: Sets whether the pattern changes when a program change message is received.

action: AIRA LINK for the MX-1
goal: Turn on AIRA LINK when the S-1 is connected to an MX-1 mixer over USB.
caveat: Takes effect after the power is turned off and on again; otherwise leave it Off.

citation.quote: Set this to “On” when connecting a device via USB that is compatible with AIRA LINK, such as the MX-1.

action: Power up in battery-only mode
goal: Run from the internal battery, e.g. when connected to an iOS device with a Lightning adapter.

citation.quote: This powers up the unit in battery-only mode.

action: Master tune (433–448 Hz)
goal: Tune the whole instrument to other gear or a recording.

citation.quote: Sets the master tuning.

action: Set the USB audio level independently
goal: Record into a DAW at a fixed level regardless of the VOLUME knob.

citation.quote: Configures the volume of the signal output to USB.

action: Set the keyboard pads’ velocity
goal: Choose the fixed velocity (1–127) the keyboard pads play and record.

citation.quote: Sets the keyboard velocity.
